messages:
mira: Heads up  EU-west3 nvme pool `scratch-hot-7` is spiking IOPS and causing GPU attach delays/fails. Seeing a bunch of attach timeouts and backlog in the scheduler. :eyes:
ryan: Can you paste a quick iostat or top of the IO queue? thinking janitor scrub overlap again.
mira: iostat from one of the affected hosts (short):
```
Device: rrqm/s wrqm/s r/s w/s rkB/s wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await svctm %util
nvme0n1: 0.00 0.00 18.00 980.00 288.00 8200.00 8.50 15.20 12.1 1.10 99.9
nvme1n1: 0.00 0.00 10.00 860.00 160.00 7100.00 8.30 12.10 11.3 1.05 98.4
```
mira: scheduler backlog metric `gpu.attach.latency.p95` jumped from 120ms -> 2.3s after midnight. lots of `attach_timeout` errors in logs.
ryan: Ugh. This looks like janitor scrub/trim floods when the cleaner window overlapped a batch release. Suggest temporary QoS throttling for janitor on that pool + route new GPU attaches to fallback pool. Keep io-sla tight for live attaches.
olga: What's the cost & impact of moving a subset of GPUs to a reserved pool vs throttling? need numbers for finance if we opt to reserve capacity. :money_with_wings:
sam: quick mitigation I can push now  reduce janitor concurrency + add soft io-limit on scratch-hot-7. Patch snippet below (will run as immediate canary on 10 nodes):
```yaml
janitor:
  pools:
    scratch-hot-7:
      concurrency: 6  # was 24
      io_limit_mb_s: 120  # soft throttle for scrub jobs
```
redwoodctl apply --cluster eu-west3 --patch janitor/scratch-hot-7.yaml --scope canary:10
```
engjanitor-bot: Adjustments applied: concurrency=6, io_limit_mb_s=120 for pool "scratch-hot-7". Canary rollout to 10 hosts started. Monitoring hooks added.
mira: After the canary rollout attach failures dropped to near-zero and `gpu.attach.latency.p95` fell to ~180ms. Good sign. :thumbsup:
ryan: Good. Next steps: open a follow-up ticket to evaluate longer-term options  1) adjust janitor cadence, 2) migrate noisy workloads to a dedicated scratch pool, or 3) reserve 20 GPUs in dedicated-eu-west3 for high-SLO jobs.
olga: For budgeting: moving 20 GPUs to reserved would be ~ $12k/month (back-of-envelope), but avoids repeated firefights and reduces tail latency for customers. If we only reserve 10 as a pilot reduces to ~ $6k/month. I'll sync with finance.
sam: I'll open the PR for the janitor change + a runbook step to automatically divert attaches when `nvme.util` > 85% for >5m. Command I'm going to use now to shift 10 nodes: `redwoodctl allocate --pool reserved-eu-west3 --count 10 --tag noisy-nvme-fallback`
mira: Watching dashboards: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/d/attach-health/eu-west3?orgId=1  will report back in 30m if anything flares.
ryan: Filing ticket ENGINFRA-4821 to track follow-ups and cost decision. Assigning to @sam and @olga.
mira: thanks all  mitigated for now, but we should automate the divert + alerting thresholds so this doesn't need manual ops next time. :heavy_check_mark:
